body: local.WithDurability(DurabilityFull|DurabilityFile|DurabilityNone). Default Full: the staged file is fsynced before the rename and the directories whose entries the rename (and any newly created parents) changed are fsynced after, as renameio and databases do, so a write that returned survives a crash or power cut. File (the previous behaviour) fsyncs only the bytes, so a crash can bring back the old version or lose a new key; None syncs nothing, for caches/scratch/tests. Safe default because callers assume a returned write is durable; the cost is one extra directory fsync per write. Directory sync is skipped on Windows. A Move is durable at its destination only (the source dir may have been pruned). (2026-10-08, IN-10)
title: Local driver defaults to DurabilityFull (fsync file and directories)
